rubric_items.reason: All the changed design parts are in the code: the NO_SHOW sub-select with $4/$2 bounds, noShows in the api and web types, the No-shows tile after Cancelled with the NO_SHOW period link, and both tests updated.
The code follows the existing local patterns. The count SQL stays in DashboardService, not a repository as conventions say. The design accepted this trade-off on purpose.
Five files, all named by the design components. Every edit is additive and the other sub-selects, tiles and fields are untouched.
No new endpoint. Period validation is reused. Edge cases are tested: no No-shows (0), inside Today, outside the next day's Today and inside Last 7 days. The tile link total matches the count.
The summary and the Changes list match the diff in each of the five files, including test names and fixture values.

findings.text: The No-show count adds SQL to DashboardService, but conventions put SQL in api/src/repositories. The design accepted this local precedent, so this is a note only.

cites.quote: (SELECT count(*) FROM appointment WHERE status = 'NO_SHOW' AND starts_at >= $4 AND starts_at < $2) AS no_shows

findings.text: The new API test changes shared state (it marks the 09:30 appointment No-show and moves the clock) and depends on running last. Reordering the tests or running them in parallel would break the earlier exact assertions.

cites.quote: // Runs last: it closes today's 09:30 appointment as No-show and moves the clock.

findings.suggested_fix: Give the HMS-3 case its own fixture or describe block with its own database, or reset the clock and state afterwards.
